From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood + FinMatch

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the honest conversation. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard
- Primary objective: reduce per-transaction inference cost for FinMatch’s fraud-detection alerts while keeping 99th percentile latency under 120ms for high-priority flows.
- Current constraints: on-prem data retention requirements for EU-origin customers (you mentioned a hybrid deployment might be required), and procurement timeline targeting Q1 2027.

Success signals
- 20–30% reduction in inference unit cost vs current setup
- No functional regressions on alert quality (same or better precision/recall on the 3 red-flag prompt set)
- Signed pilot contract for Dedicated capacity + SOC2 evidence for security review

Next steps (proposed)
1) Technical sync (30–45m) with your infra/infra-security + our runtime team — cover network/KMS and deployment options (VPC vs dedicated). Proposed slots: Mon 10/25 10:00 or Tue 10/26 14:00 PT.
2) I’ll share the discovery notes and a short briefing deck with architecture options (attached).
3) If we align, we’ll scope a 6–8 week pilot (Dedicated capacity, targeted load profile) and provide a temporary SLA for the pilot window.

Attachments: FinMatch-discovery-notes.pdf (notes from today), Redwood-briefing-deck.pdf (options + rough costing).

If the dates above don’t work send a couple of times that do and Alex or I will coordinate.

Thanks — speak soon,

Vanessa Ortiz
